blocks.text: Real-world basis: The Alps, Himalayas, Andes, Caucasus, and transhumance routes.
Landscape: A high pass is marked by bell-shaped relay structures that answer travelers with tones indicating weather, route stability, and body compatibility.

Mini timeline: Era Zero — A Pilgrim World establishes the pass as a place where travelers adapt bodies gradually to altitude and cold. Era One — Faster standardized bodies make the acclimation villages seem obsolete. Era Two — The pass remains because abrupt translation would destroy several small-bodied species and cultural practices. Era Three — Bell meanings survive more reliably than their grammar. Some tones warn of avalanche; others once indicated consent requirements for entering a destination. Confusing the two can be dangerous in different ways.
Present condition: Maintained by Pathkeepers who test routes through embodied travel rather than trusting old charts alone.

Aesthetic brief: Snow peaks, dark pines, stone switchbacks, prayer-flag-like signal strips without copying a single human culture, and bronze-white relay bells embedded in cliffs. Corrupted bells produce visible concentric air patterns that point toward the wrong pass.
Background profile: Freezing-Cold; Dry to Moist; alpine pass; disciplined, communal, exposed; high rock friction and low ice friction.
